title: Govern disaster recovery activation and coordination
question: Who may declare DR, set restoration priority, communicate, validate, and accept the recovered business service when the primary channel is unavailable?
scenario: A regional outage affects identity, network, and application services. The operations lead wants to declare DR, while the business owner has not confirmed which customer functions must be restored first.
focalRelation: incident authority --declares disaster--> DR coordinator business owner --sets priority and accepts service--> restoration sequence technical teams --restore and evidence--> validators communications lead --authenticated message and audience control--> stakeholders primary channel failure --preplanned alternate channel--> coordination

nodes.detail: Impact to identity, network, and applications with business priorities not yet confirmed.

states.title: Case facts fixed
states.caption: A regional outage affects identity, network, and application services. The operations lead wants to declare DR, while the business owner has not confirmed which customer functions must be restored first.

states.title: Controlling condition identified
states.caption: Declaration authority and activation criteria should be defined before an event.

states.title: Tempting shortcut rejected
states.caption: The technical team can declare and prioritize DR alone. Technical evidence informs the decision, but business authority and continuity priorities determine which services and risks are accepted.

statuses.n4: technical recovery cannot choose business priority

states.title: Bounded action applied
states.caption: Use the defined declaration criteria, record the uncertainty, activate the recovery authority, and obtain the business priority decision while technical teams assess dependencies. Use out-of-band communication if the normal channel is affected, restrict emergency access, and document the assumptions that will be revisited during restoration.

states.title: Outcome accepted with limits
states.caption: Given a disruptive event, coordinate declaration, response, personnel, communications, assessment, training, and lessons ownership without confusing technical recovery with business acceptance. The case record retains the scope, owner, exceptions, and evidence used for this conclusion.

variants.label: Changed case
variants.changedFact: The primary crisis bridge is unavailable, and a supplier requests privileged credentials by email to accelerate recovery.

states.title: Changed case fact isolated
states.caption: The primary crisis bridge is unavailable, and a supplier requests privileged credentials by email to accelerate recovery.

statuses.n5: primary bridge unavailable; email credential request

states.title: Decision recomputed
states.caption: Use the approved out-of-band channel, verify supplier identity and authority, issue bounded emergency access through the controlled process, and record the decision. Pressure and unavailable systems do not remove the need for authenticated communication and least privilege.

statuses.n5: supplier identity verified out of band

states.title: Changed outcome verified
states.caption: The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.

prediction.prompt: Who may declare DR, set restoration priority, communicate, validate, and accept the recovered business service when the primary channel is unavailable?

options.label: Use declared DR authority and obtain the business restoration priority
options.feedback: Correct for this scenario: this answer uses the displayed relation and preserves its scope. Technical evidence informs the decision, but business authority and continuity priorities determine which services and risks are accepted.

options.label: The technical team can declare and prioritize DR alone.
options.feedback: Incorrect: Technical evidence informs the decision, but business authority and continuity priorities determine which services and risks are accepted.

options.label: Let the operations lead declare DR and set customer restoration order without business confirmation.
options.feedback: Incorrect: technical urgency does not confer every decision right. Use the declared authority, alternate communications, business priorities, status ownership, validation, and acceptance roles.

prediction.hint: Name the controlling relationship and the point where its result must be enforced; do not rely on a label or successful prior step.

retry.prompt: The primary declaration officer is unreachable and the succession list has not been tested in two years. What should the recovery team do?

options.label: Let the most senior technician declare the disaster because action is urgent
options.feedback: Technical seniority does not automatically carry business declaration authority.

options.label: Take no protective action until the primary officer is found, even if delay increases harm
options.feedback: The plan should permit bounded protective action and alternate authority; a missing path is a governance defect to escalate.

options.label: Invoke approved alternate authority, record it, and later test the succession path
options.feedback: Correct. A predefined alternate preserves accountable declaration under degraded conditions.

retry.hint: Recovery authority needs an approved alternate path; urgency does not allow the team to invent one.

takeaway: Use the defined declaration criteria, record the uncertainty, activate the recovery authority, and obtain the business priority decision while technical teams assess dependencies.
assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The decision graph preserves declaration authority, business priority ownership, technical recovery roles, out-of-band communications, credential limits, and an attributable decision/assumption log. It omits the reviewed responsibility swimlane and message-lane geometry, so the mechanism is equivalent.

learningJob.plainExplanation: Technical evidence informs disaster declaration, but defined authority and business priorities govern activation and restoration order. Alternate communications and bounded emergency access are required when the normal channel is unavailable.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: The observed responsibility lanes let the learner compare declaration authority, business priority, technical assessment, alternate communication, and acceptance ownership.
